headline_marked: Mexico-England World Cup match [[delayed by one hour due to storms]] in Mexico City
headline: Mexico-England World Cup match delayed by one hour due to storms in Mexico City
summary: The FIFA World Cup last-16 clash between Mexico and England faced a one-hour delay at Estadio Azteca. Heavy rain and thunder storms in Mexico City prompted the decision to ensure safety.
details: England's World Cup last-16 match against Mexico has been delayed by one hour due to severe weather in Mexico City. FIFA confirmed the decision on Sunday, with the match at Estadio Azteca now set to kick off at 7:00 am (Bangladesh time).

Thunderstorms and heavy rain lashed Mexico City, leading to concerns about lightning risk near the stadium. FIFA stated that the safety and security of all individuals is their priority, thanking fans for their understanding.

This isn't the first weather-related disruption for Mexico at the Azteca; their round of 32 win over Ecuador was also delayed by stormy conditions. FIFA had previously discussed moving the match forward by six hours to avoid potential storms.

However, after consulting both teams, FIFA ultimately decided to stick with the planned kick-off time, only to delay it by an hour. England hopes the sodden conditions might dampen the fervent home support.
Mexico boasts an impressive home record, having won all four tournament games on home soil without conceding a goal. They have also lost just twice in 89 matches at the iconic Estadio Azteca.
